title: deal channel v2 — schema-first (AFB backend<->AFB frontend only; not part of afb.execution.v1 wire)
description: Negotiated via auth.support/auth_ok.support (capability id afbws.deal.channel.v2). Same convention as afbws.alarm/account/tradeplan v2: ONE schema id per message (`afbws.deal.<op>.v2`, no .request/.response/.push suffixes); the same schema is the request and its response (a response echoes `request_id`); server pushes (`record`, `outcome`, `event`, `pnl`, `triggered`) are the same kind of message without `request_id`. State and facts are split: `record` is the authoritative state of a deal, `outcome` the result of a command, `event` a thin allow-listed fact for the feed (typed per event, see $defs/event), `pnl` the periodic unrealized P&L, `triggered` the guaranteed notifications (acked with `ack`). Strict (additionalProperties:false), no legacy forms: `status`/`execution_phase` are the shared enums (common.v1.json#/$defs/dealStatus, executionPhase), `error.details` does not exist (the server populates none). `item`/`items`/`results` never carry the persisted DealState file shape (source_refs, status_history, event_journal, raw orders/positions, observed) — see $defs/dealSummary and $defs/dealDetail, explicit allow-list projections built by backend/trade/public_views.py. publish/rebind/amend resolve the source tradeplan only via the deal's own link (deal.public.v1.json source.tradeplan_id); they never accept an inline plan-like draft. See AFB/docs/ws/deal.md.

dealResultStatus.description: Status in an operation/publish result row: the deal status after the command, or `deleted` right after `delete` (the deal is archived and no longer exists as a record).

dealSizingDisplay.title: Broker-sizing display projection (lots/required_cash/...) needed by the Deals widget row/editor — not the raw compiled sizing block.

resolved_lots.description: BF-resolved actual order quantity (lots), fixed once at entry-trigger time — distinct from `lots`, which stays the pre-trade publish estimate. Present only once BF has reported it (`status_changed.quantity`).

dealOpenPosition.title: AFB-computed open position of the deal — the same source ladder as the pnl push's qty+avg_price (backend/trade/pnl.py resolve_open_qty/resolve_open_avg), never the raw orders[]/positions[]/observed.
dealOpenPosition.description: Absent entirely means flat (no open position) or not yet known — distinct from a present qty of 0, which is never emitted.

qty.description: Signed net quantity (positive long, negative short).

avg_price.description: Decimal string — weighted-average open entry price.

as_of.description: ISO-8601 timestamp this snapshot was computed at.

dealRealizedPnl.title: AFB-computed realized P&L (rubles), projected from the internal afb_pnl ledger — never the raw ledger itself.
dealRealizedPnl.description: Absent entirely means no ledger yet (deal predates it, or has not had an exit fill) — distinct from a present-but-degraded value.

value.description: Decimal string, rubles. Null exactly when degraded is set — a fill's money multiplier (step_price/price_step or lot_size) could not be resolved.

dealSummary.title: Minimal row/card projection for list — no compiled deal body, no source_refs, no journals.
dealSummary.description: Explicit allow-list built by backend/trade/public_views.py::deal_summary, never a serialization of the persisted DealState (source_refs, status_history, event_journal, raw orders/positions, observed, owner_user_id never appear). `sizing` is the user-set {mode,value} from the «Риск и объём» block — NOT the broker_sizing projection, see `broker_sizing`.

instrument_key.description: Full catalog key of the deal's instrument. Optional: absent on deals stored before the key existed.

dealDetail.title: Full editor payload — dealSummary + the compiled public deal + the phase-B amendability projection.
dealDetail.description: Allow-list built by backend/trade/public_views.py::deal_detail. `deal` is the public afb.deal.v2 projection (deal.public.v1.json). `editable_fields` lists what the current status/execution_phase allows to amend.

instrument_key.description: Full catalog key of the deal's instrument. Optional: absent on deals stored before the key existed.

dealLegEdit.title: Edit of one EXISTING leg, by its current index in the deal's role array — never by leg_id (the deal side has no leg_id).

dealNewLeg.title: A brand-new deal-only leg (no linked tradeplan leg) — appended at the end of the role's array.

dealRoleEdit.title: Per-role (entry/stop_loss/take_profit) leg-level edit fragment.
dealRoleEdit.description: Indices refer to the CURRENT deal's leg array for that role at base_revision — never a tradeplan's, never leg_id. edited/removed_indices/reset_indices apply to existing legs; new_legs are appended after them. See AFB backend tradeplans/overrides.py::apply_deal_edit for the exact merge order.

reset_indices.description: Drop this leg's deal-level override (source reverts to tradeplan) — the leg re-adopts whatever the linked plan currently holds for the matching leg_id.

dealEdit.title: Amend fragment (afbws.deal.amend.v2#/deal_edit) — per-role leg edits plus whole-value sizing/execution_policy (replace wholesale, no partial-field merge).

dealResult.title: Per-deal outcome of a publish/rebind/operation command.
dealResult.description: accepted=true: `bf_id` and `status` are set (status is `deleted` after a delete), `revision` is the deal's revision and `item` the authoritative record when the deal still exists. accepted=false: only `message` (why) — the command did not touch the deal, so there is no status/revision. When a rebind changes the deal id, `deal_id`/`item` carry the NEW id — the client must drop the old cache key.

orderRole.description: Role of an order / of the leg whose condition fired. Superset of deal_state.v2 order.role: `external_close` is the synthetic order BF records when the position was closed outside the deal (it emits order.* for it too).

orderEventStatus.description: Order status carried by an order.* event: deal_state.v2 order.status plus `unknown` (a broker answer BF could not map; BF then verifies the order against the broker).

createdData.title: deal.created — the deal record was created (publish).
createdData.description: Light, no snapshot: the full state arrives as `afbws.deal.record.v2`. Produced by AFB (no `at`).

amendedData.title: deal.amended — an amend was applied optimistically on the AFB side.
amendedData.description: Light, no snapshot (state: `afbws.deal.record.v2`; BF confirmation: `accepted`/`rejected` events and `afbws.deal.outcome.v2`). Produced by AFB (no `at`).

command_type.description: Type of the accepted AFB command (`deal.publish`, `deal.operation`, `deal.amend`, `deal.resync`, ...).

at.description: ISO-8601 BF event-occurrence time (BF `at`). Absent on events produced by AFB itself.

rejectedData.title: deal.rejected — BF rejected a command or an execution step.

message.description: Message exactly as received from BF.

command_type.description: Absent for rejections not caused by an AFB command (the broker rejected the entry order).

at.description: ISO-8601 BF event-occurrence time (BF `at`). Absent on events produced by AFB itself.

statusChangedData.title: deal.status_changed — the deal status (and/or execution phase) changed.

cancel_reason.description: Why the deal was cancelled/paused (BF user-kind or `execution_error`, ...). Only with a cancelling status.

quantity.description: Resolved order quantity (lots), fixed once by BF at entry-trigger time.

at.description: ISO-8601 BF event-occurrence time (BF `at`). Absent on events produced by AFB itself.

statusChangedData.description: Deletion/archival is NOT a status: it is the `deleted` event.

deletedData.title: deal.deleted — the deal was deleted/archived (replaces the legacy status_changed{status:deleted}).

at.description: ISO-8601 BF event-occurrence time (BF `at`). Absent on events produced by AFB itself.

reportFill.title: One broker trade of the closing report (trade-based fill log).

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 fill time, null for legacy BF versions.

reportData.title: deal.report — the closing report of the deal.

fills.description: The chart-marker source (one element per broker trade). The realized P&L is NOT here: it is `realized_pnl` of the deal record (AFB ledger).

at.description: ISO-8601 BF event-occurrence time (BF `at`). Absent on events produced by AFB itself.

ordersSyncedData.title: deal.orders_synced — BF reconciled the deal's orders with the broker.

at.description: ISO-8601 BF event-occurrence time (BF `at`). Absent on events produced by AFB itself.

ordersSyncedData.description: Marker event: the changed orders arrive as separate order.* events and in the record.

positionsSyncedData.title: deal.positions_synced — BF reconciled the deal's positions with the broker.

at.description: ISO-8601 BF event-occurrence time (BF `at`). Absent on events produced by AFB itself.

positionsSyncedData.description: Marker event (declared by the BF protocol; current BF versions do not emit it).

order_id.description: BF's own client_order_id — the identity to match orders by.

price.description: Limit/stop price, or the average fill price once filled. Decimal string, null when unknown.

at.description: ISO-8601 BF event-occurrence time (BF `at`). Absent on events produced by AFB itself.

broker_order_id.description: The broker's own exchange order id, when known.

orderData.title: order.filled / order.partially_filled / order.cancelled / order.rejected — an order changed its status.

order_id.description: BF's own client_order_id — the identity to match orders by.

price.description: Limit/stop price, or the average fill price once filled. Decimal string, null when unknown.

at.description: ISO-8601 BF event-occurrence time (BF `at`). Absent on events produced by AFB itself.

positionData.title: position.opened / position.changed / position.closed — the deal's net position changed.

symbol.description: Instrument symbol of the position (the key of the client's per-deal position map): the broker symbol, else the bare ticker.

quantity.description: Signed net quantity after the change; 0 on closed.

at.description: ISO-8601 BF event-occurrence time (BF `at`). Absent on events produced by AFB itself.

phase.description: Role of the leg whose condition fired (BF `phase`).

at.description: ISO-8601 BF event-occurrence time (BF `at`). Absent on events produced by AFB itself.

event.title: afbws.deal.event.v2 — one trading/lifecycle event of a deal (server push, no request_id), typed by (category, event).
event.description: A thin, allow-listed event for the event feed, the order/position patches and the chart markers — never a state snapshot (state: `afbws.deal.record.v2`) and never a raw BF payload: only the fields a consumer reads or that make up the meaning of the event are listed, everything else BF sends (`broker_instrument`, `validation`, `execution_legs`, `target_instrument_patch`, `binding`, `snapshot`, `observed`, `deal.snapshot` altogether) is dropped. `data` is determined by `event` within `category`; `category` is fixed per event.

triggerReportData.title: report notification payload — the closing summary without the fill log.

triggerStatusChanged.title: Guaranteed notification: the deal status changed.

triggerRejected.title: Guaranteed notification: BF rejected a command or an execution step.

triggerReport.title: Guaranteed notification: the closing report of the deal.

triggerEvent.title: afb.deal.trigger.v2 — one guaranteed deal notification, typed by `event` (the MAIL_DEAL_EVENTS set).
triggerEvent.description: Schema analogue of the legacy TriggeredDealItem — not the MQTT notification.deal.v1 payload (different transport). `notification_id` is the idempotency key the client acks.

get.title: afbws.deal.get.v2 — read one deal (request / response).
get.description: Request: `deal_id`. Response (same `request_id`): `item`. Exactly one of the two.

list.title: afbws.deal.list.v2 — read the caller's deals (request / response).
list.description: Request: no filters (the plan->deals grouping is built from `tradeplan_id` of each row, not a server-side filter). Response (same `request_id`): `items[]`.

publish.title: afbws.deal.publish.v2 — publish an already-saved tradeplan as a deal (request / response).
publish.description: Request: `tradeplan_id` + `bf_id` (no inline plan draft, no plural bf_ids — 1:1). Response (same `request_id`): `results[]` (batch-shaped, at most one element today) and `accepted`. Distinguished by `results`: present => response, absent => request.

rebind.title: afbws.deal.rebind.v2 — move a deal to another connector (request / response).
rebind.description: Request: `deal_id` + `bf_id` (the backend resolves the source tradeplan via the deal's own link). Response (same `request_id`): `results[]` and `accepted`; if the new target changes the deal id, `results[0].deal_id`/`item` carry the NEW id. Distinguished by `results`.

operation.title: afbws.deal.operation.v2 — lifecycle commands over deals (request / response).
operation.description: Request: `items[]` (at least one). Response (same `request_id`): `results[]` (one per item, partial failures are rows with accepted=false) and `accepted`. Distinguished by `items` vs `results`.

amend.title: afbws.deal.amend.v2 — per-leg amend of a deal (request / response).
amend.description: Request: `deal_id`, optional `deal_edit` (only the legs/fields overridden on the deal side; anything omitted keeps following the linked tradeplan) and optional `base_revision` (optimistic concurrency: a mismatch is a `conflict` error carrying the current `item`). Response (same `request_id`): `item` (authoritative record), `revision`, `status`, `accepted`. The outcome of the BF confirmation arrives later as `outcome` and `event` pushes. Distinguished by `item`.

ack.title: afbws.deal.ack.v2 — acknowledge delivered notifications (request / response).
ack.description: Request: `events[]` (afb.deal.trigger_ack.v2), at least one. Response (same `request_id`): `results[]` — one per event, `status` ok | not_found. Exactly one of `events` / `results`.

error.title: afbws.deal.error.v2 — typed error for a whole request (server -> client).
error.description: `item` (the authoritative current record) is only present with `conflict` — a stale `base_revision` on amend — so the client can adopt it instead of retrying blind; a `conflict` may also come without it (lifecycle/amend gate, deal id taken). No other code carries `item`, and no code carries `details`: the server populates none for the deal channel.

record.title: afbws.deal.record.v2 — authoritative state of one deal (server push, no request_id).
record.description: REPLACE of the public projection identified by deal_id: the client overwrites its cached copy, never merges. One push per mutation of the record. It carries NO command outcome — that is `afbws.deal.outcome.v2`; and no thin events are merged into it — see `afbws.deal.event.v2`.

outcome.title: afbws.deal.outcome.v2 — outcome of a command or an execution step (server push, no request_id).
outcome.description: A separate push, so the client does not need the whole record just to show a toast. AFB composes no user-facing texts: it passes through what BF returned, the text is built on the frontend. result=rejected: any BF rejection (`code` required). result=accepted: only the confirmation of `deal.amend` (the one accepted outcome the server reports), without code/message/broker_error.

command.description: Command type this outcome refers to (`deal.amend`, `deal.publish`, `deal.operation`, `deal.resync`, ...), null for an outcome not caused by a command (an execution rejection).

code.description: Rejection code from BF `deal.rejected.code`. Only with result=rejected.

message.description: Message exactly as received from BF. Only with result=rejected.

pnl.title: afbws.deal.pnl.v2 — periodic unrealized P&L of an open deal (server push, no request_id).
pnl.description: Not persisted. `trend` is deliberately absent — a frontend-only projection computed from consecutive pushes.

triggered.title: afbws.deal.triggered.v2 — guaranteed deal notifications (server push, no request_id).
triggered.description: Server-initiated; same ack discipline as alarms: a reconnect redelivers events that were not acked (afbws.deal.ack.v2).
